## Configuration and switch evidence {#sec-ch15-ch12-tests}

This catalogue accompanies @sec-ch12-matrix. The source pin is
`snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0`.
No snapy executable, installed snapy package, CUDA test or multi-rank test was run for this draft.
“Registered” below describes source evidence, not a measured pass.

### Independent report checks

The command `python src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.py` runs exact rational/symbolic identities
on CPU without importing snapy. The committed output is
`src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.out`. The pytest wrapper is `src/tests/test_ch12_checks.py`.

| output label | assertion | tolerance | what it does not establish |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[C1]` | 18 parser cases and 8 implication cases | exact truth table | execution of C++ static caching |
| `[C2]` | filter, wall continuation and face moments | exact rational zero | measured solver order |
| `[C3]` | five spherical moments and six pressure identities | exact symbolic zero | compiled geometry/ghost behavior |
| `[C4]` | covariance, mass-weighted mean and shared-face cancellation | exact symbolic zero | nonlinear MC accuracy or MPI exchange |
| `[C5]` | energy increment cancels the change of corrected potential energy | exact symbolic zero | limiter, solid and implicit implementation |

: Independent checks and their limits. {#tbl-ch15-ch12-independent}

The ghost-depth rejection and zero-gravity exception are included with the seam tests. A CTest filter must execute
its one selected assertion; registration's pass marker guards against an empty filter. Positive mass-covariance
accuracy remains missing even though its minimum-cell guard is present.

: Source thresholds are acceptance criteria, not observed values. {#tbl-ch15-ch12-numerical}

The three rows marked "main after chengcli/snapy#303" describe main at chengcli/snapy `9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97`, while the rest of this table is pinned at `e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0`. Their ctest names are `test_flux_covariance_seams_python`, `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_flux_covariance_python` and `test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact`, `_radial_exact_off` with their `test_x1_seam_split_mp_` counterparts. Their status is the one the body of chengcli/snapy#303 states: CPU `ctest -j1` 114 of 115 on the branch (the body does not name the commit of that run, so it is not shown to include every row marked here), the one failure `test_straka` (no `pd-combine` on that machine); the radial-exact gap at $n_1$ = 32, 64, 128 went from $8.0\times10^{-7}$, $6.3\times10^{-8}$, $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to 0; the covariance arm on the panel seams passes at the head ($2.4\times10^{-15}$ against $10^{-13}$) and fails with the panel-seam change reverted ($5.03\times10^{-10}$), the two-valued dry-mass seam faces going from 288/576 (as the body gives them) to 0 [source: chengcli/snapy#303 body; sha: snapy@546b1afd80d47a437a92ead745ef525f8335094a (PR head); deck/run: the ctest arms named, CPU `ctest -j1`; the commit of the CPU run and the devices of the gaps not stated in the body]. Its CUDA run (RTX 5090), at snapy@f5c0cff427db4681d0e65e40ae5a88c974e1a617, gave the switch-on gap exactly 0 and a switch-off gap of $1.9\times10^{-14}$ at $n_1=128$, which is why the switch-off arm is bounded by $10^{-13}$ rather than 0 [source: chengcli/snapy#303 body; sha: snapy@f5c0cff427db4681d0e65e40ae5a88c974e1a617; deck/run: CUDA `ctest -j1` on an RTX 5090]. The observed numbers in this paragraph are the body's, not acceptance criteria.

The tolerance choices separate roundoff budgets, deliberate nonzero controls and discretization-order thresholds.
They are the pinned tests' contracts, not new tolerance recommendations. Read @sec-ch12-matrix for the exact names
and environment of each arm. The two-rank registration does not turn the FC panel test into an MPI test.

### Reproduction and missing evidence

Use a CPU-only build for new configuration evidence. Record the full source pin, cache options, package import
origin, test name, complete scheme environment, device, precision and rank count with each result. First run the
import-path and setup tests, then the desired numerical arms in fresh processes. The model used by a Python
assertion must come from the intended checkout rather than an unrelated installed package.

No build is required for the exact report identities. Official citation checking and HTML/PDF rendering remain
pending because the frozen tree has neither the official checker nor the book skeleton, and Quarto is not installed.
The chapter provides scheme includes for editor integration rather than modifying editor-owned chapter/configuration files.
Missing combinations are numerical MC; XC+face/RE; XC+FC; WB/XC gnomonic; WB+face with RE off; and FC across ranks.

The two-rank assertions are `split_across_two_ranks_matches_one_process` in {{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split_mp.cpp X1SeamSplitMp.split_across_two_ranks_matches_one_process >}}.
